# Requirements

What Siklab Core needs to run, and where it is proven. The support levels are literal:
**stable** means we test it on every release; **beta** means it ships and works but is not
covered by that testing. We would rather tell you which is which than claim a matrix we
have not earned.

---

## Operating systems

| Platform | Support | What that means here |
|---|---|---|
| macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon) | **Stable** | Tested on every release. |
| macOS (Intel) | Beta | Ships and works, but is not covered by our per-release testing. |
| Linux (arm64) | Beta | Install, start-up, sign-in and the interface are all proven. A full end-to-end build has not been. |
| Linux (x86-64) | Beta | Installed successfully by a beta tester on real WSL. Needs a CPU with AVX2 — the app refuses to start with a named error if yours lacks it. |
| Windows (via WSL2) | Beta | Runs the same Linux build. Does not restart by itself after a reboot — start it again from your WSL terminal. |
| Windows | Not supported | There is no native Windows build. Use WSL2. |

!!! note "On Linux and WSL"
    On Linux and WSL the agents build normally, but the browser-backed verification steps need Chromium system libraries. Siklab installs them where it has permission and tells you the exact command when it does not.

---

## An AI engine (you supply this)

You supply the AI. Siklab Core contains no AI model and no API key, and never sees or stores your provider credentials.

**Recommended: `claude` or `codex`.** In practice these two are the most stable. Others in the list below work but throw provider errors more often, which shows up as a build that stalls or stops.

**Also supported:** `codex`, `claude`, `agy`, `openclaw`, `opencode`, `qwen`, `pi`, `ollama`, `aider`.

!!! warning "Known unstable"
    `agy`, `opencode`, `qwen` throw provider errors more often than
    the others. The symptom is a build that appears to stall or stop for no reason. If that
    happens repeatedly, switch engine in **Settings → Engines** before assuming Siklab is at
    fault — it usually is not.

An API key can be used instead of a CLI — Anthropic-, OpenAI- or Google-shaped endpoints, set in Settings → Engines. Keys are stored encrypted on your machine.

## Where things live

| | |
|---|---|
| The app | `~/.siklab-core` |
| Your data | `~/.siklab` |
| Opens at | `http://localhost:3200` |
| Your finished apps | ~/.siklab/workspaces/&lt;project&gt;, with studio artefacts in ~/.siklab/vault/studio |

Ordinary folders, ordinary files. Nothing is locked, encrypted, or in a proprietary format.

## Before you buy anything

The trial is 3 days, bound to one machine, with no card and no account. **It starts on your first build** — NOT on download and NOT on install. You can install today and start the clock next week.

When it ends: Everything you already built stays yours and stays usable: open it, run it, export it. A plan is needed only to START something new.

---

## What Siklab does not do

- Deploy or host your applications for you
- Provide an AI subscription
- Work without an AI CLI or API key that you supply

## What is not guaranteed

- Generated code can be wrong, insecure, incomplete, or unsuitable for your purpose.
- Browser verification checks the flows it was asked to check. It is not proof the app has no bugs, and it is not a security review.
- Generated code may resemble other code that exists in the world.

**Review and test anything you build before relying on it, publishing it, or putting it in front of anyone else.** Anyone claiming an AI tool produces guaranteed
production-ready software is selling something. Siklab tells you what it checked and what
it did not, and the rest is your call.

---

## Known limitations

The current honest list, kept here rather than left for you to discover:

- Linux and WSL are beta: a full end-to-end build has not been verified on either.
- macOS on Intel ships but is not covered by our per-release testing.
- Unstable AI CLIs (notably agy, opencode) can throw provider errors mid-build; use claude or codex if a build keeps stalling.
- There is no uninstaller script yet.
- No native Windows build exists.

Something not covered here? **support@siklabcore.com** — within 2 business days, Philippine time (UTC+8).
